method: From Kalshi legs priced 30–85¢ with edge ≥ about −2.5 and no flags (one per game), a leg was kept only when at least two of these agreed and none disagreed: Polymarket's top sports traders on its side, a published expert pick or model read today, and concrete news/matchup reasoning. The dump's expert matching came back empty again, so experts were matched by hand against picks/latest.json. Two legs (Oilers, Cincinnati) sit at about −2.8, slightly past the usual limit, kept because the evidence was clean; Duke and Kansas rest on one expert (Seth Davis) plus his reasoning. Dropped as conflicts: Bills Under 44.5 and Over 44.5 (Covers/Pickswise under, CBS's model over, top traders on the over), Cavaliers/Hornets spreads and moneyline (Predictem on Cleveland -8.5, Covers on Charlotte, top traders on the Hornets +8.5), Lakers/Hawks spread and moneyline (Dimers and Bleacher Nation on the Lakers, Covers and top traders on Atlanta), Grizzlies/Raptors moneyline (TheLines vs Covers), Pacers/Mavericks moneyline (Covers on Indiana, top traders and Dimers' model on Dallas) and total (TheLines and Dimers' model on the over, the only positive edge on the under), Warriors spread (Covers on Golden State, top traders on New Orleans +6.5), Flyers/Canucks moneyline (Dimers vs Bleacher Nation), Ohio/Miami (TheRX on Ohio, Dimers on Miami), Illinois/Texas Tech (Davis on Illinois, priced at −5.5 edge). The ladder is shorter than usual at 8 because few legs cleared the bar, and it fills in Tuesday's games late.
honest: Every leg costs slightly more than fair, so expected return is slightly negative and gets worse with every leg added.

ladder.label: Buffalo Bills
ladder.why: Biggest money among the legs that cleared the bar: top traders ≈$41.1k for, ≈$22.0k against. FOX's Schwartz and Pickswise's Farley back Buffalo, citing the Bills' No. 1 scoring offense (33.3 ppg) against a Vikings attack starting Carson Wentz for injured Kyler Murray. Caution: Buffalo's offensive line is hurt, and Yahoo and ClutchPoints take the Vikings on the spread (neither has them winning outright).

ladder.label: Detroit Pistons −10.5
ladder.why: Top traders ≈$2.2k for, nothing against. Predictem's Jensen projects Pistons 113-100 and cites Detroit's league-best defense (103.6 per 100); Covers' Metler has Detroit the biggest favorite on the slate, with Anthony Davis questionable. Risk: Detroit is on a back-to-back without Jalen Duren.

ladder.label: Under 47.5
ladder.why: TheRX's Callahan and Bleacher Nation's computer both take Under 47.5; Callahan cites Akron's Under in three of four home games and two run-first teams. Bleacher Nation's own numbers do put Akron games at 50.6 points on average, so it isn't one-way. No top-trader position either way.

ladder.label: Houston Rockets
ladder.why: Top traders ≈$19.1k for, under $1k against, and the line has moved 14.6 points Houston's way. Covers and TheLines both like Houston with several Denver starters questionable; Dimers' model has Houston winning 112-105 at 74.4% (it takes Denver only on the +8.5 spread).

ladder.label: Edmonton Oilers
ladder.why: Top traders ≈$13.7k for, ≈$7.5k against. numberFire gives Edmonton 63.6% and Bleacher Nation's computer has Edmonton winning 4-3; Edmonton is 8-4 as a moneyline favorite. Priced just outside the usual edge limit (−2.78).

ladder.game: Michigan State Spartans @ Duke Blue Devils
ladder.label: Duke Blue Devils
ladder.why: Hoops HQ's Seth Davis takes Duke -6.5, arguing Michigan State is smaller and thinner up front than usual under Izzo and that "Duke is just too big and too deep." Single expert with no top-trader position, so a late leg.

ladder.label: Kansas Jayhawks
ladder.why: Davis also takes Kansas -5.5 against Kentucky, citing the Jayhawks' fifth-year transfers including Trey Kaufman-Renn and Kentucky's narrow early struggles against James Madison. Single expert with no top-trader position, so a late leg.

ladder.label: Cincinnati Bearcats
ladder.why: Dimers' Bevilacqua (79.6% to win, -6.5), Action Network's staff (-6.5 best bet, Bad Expectation Favorites system) and Bleacher Nation's computer (75-62) all land on Cincinnati, and the line moved 2.6 points its way. Priced just outside the usual edge limit (−2.77); no top-trader position.
